summary: Kimmo Koskenniemi is a linguist who studied at Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu. He was Professor of Computer Linguistics at the University of Helsinki from around 1989 to 2012 and directed its BAULT research community in 2015.
Kin Cheung works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Shigenori Nagatomo as attested in 2017.
King Chung Lo is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned a PhD from the University of Leipzig, studying under doctoral supervisor Eli Franco in 2009.
King Pong Chiu specializes in religious studies and Indology. He completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Manchester under doctoral supervisor Jacqueline Suthren Hirst, attested in 2014.

Kingsley Muthumuni de Silva was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of London around 1958 to 1961. He served as a professor at the University of Peradeniya from circa 1969 to 1995.

Kirby Flower Smith was a linguist and historian who studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University under Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve, Minton Warren, and Maurice Bloomfield. He was a professor at Johns Hopkins (~1889–1918) and directed the American Academy in Rome (1914–1915).
Kisari Mohan Ganguli was an Indology scholar who completed studies at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta.

Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who held a post at the University of Calcutta. He studied under teachers Gopinath Bhattacharya and Ashoke Kumar Gangopadhyaya, as well as several traditional teachers including Madhusudana Nyāyācārya.

Kitarō Nishida was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Tokyo Imperial University under Karl Florenz. He served as Professor of Philosophy at Kyoto University (1910–1928) and held posts at the Fourth Higher School and Gakushuin, among others.

Kiyoaki Okuda is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate under Ludwig Alsdorf around 1968–1973. He held posts as professor at International Buddhist University (attested 1993) and director at Shitennoji Doctrinal Research Institute (attested 2000).

Kiyoshi Kato was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a BA at Otani University, studying under Enga Teramoto. He worked at Higashi Honganji in 1935 and was vice-principal at Hyangsam Vocational Girls' School in 1938.
Kiyoshi Miki was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University under Kitarō Nishida around 1917–1920. He held academic posts at Otani University and Ryukoku University from around 1924 to 1927.

Kiyoshi Okano is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. At Kyushu University, he was an associate professor of humanities in 2002 and served as a professor between 2013 and 2024.

Kiyoshi Shimokawabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Rissho University. He held academic positions at Rissho University, attested in 1990 and as a special researcher in 2001.

Kiyoshi Yabuuchi was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University (~1926–1929). He later served on the faculty of Kyoto University (~1935–1969) and Ryukoku University (~1970–1979).

Kiyotaka Kimura is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, served as president of Tsurumi University (~2001–2009), and headed the Todaiji Kegon Institute.

Kiyotaka Yoshimizu is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Gerhard Oberhammer. He held academic positions at Toyo Bunko, Hokkaido University (~1996–2005), and Tohoku University as professor beginning in 2005.

Kiyozo Kazama is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Harushige Kōzu, and at the University of Vienna. He held professorial posts at Nagoya University, the University of Tokyo, and Hosei University.

Klaus Bruhn was an Indologist who studied under Ludwig Alsdorf and Walther Schubring at the University of Hamburg, earning his doctorate and habilitation. He served as Professor of Indology at the Free University of Berlin from 1966 to 1991.

Klaus Butzenberger is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Friedrich Wilhelm at the University of Munich and completed his habilitation at the Free University of Berlin. He held the chair at the University of Tübingen from 1999 to 2017.
